strings.d1.s0.name: Gateway of India
strings.d1.s0.tips: A 1924 basalt triumphal arch opposite the Taj Mahal Palace hotel. Come in the morning for pigeons and boats.
strings.d1.s1.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
strings.d1.s1.tips: The former Prince of Wales Museum: an Indo-Saracenic dome, miniature paintings and an audio guide.
strings.d1.s2.name: Kala Ghoda Art District
strings.d1.s2.tips: Galleries, the free Jehangir Art Gallery and Rhythm House. The festival is held in February.
strings.d1.s3.name: Leopold Cafe
strings.d1.s3.tips: A Parsi cafe dating from 1871 (of Shantaram fame). Order a beer and chicken tikka; the bullet marks are still on the walls.
strings.d1.s4.name: Colaba Causeway
strings.d1.s4.tips: A street market for bargaining, cheap clothes and souvenirs.
strings.d1.b0.name: Bademiya Colaba
strings.d1.b0.tips: A late-night kebab stand behind the Taj: seekh kebab and roti.
strings.d1.b1.name: Afghan Church Colaba
strings.d1.b1.tips: An 1858 church, quieter than Kala Ghoda.
strings.d2.s0.name: Elephanta Caves
strings.d2.s0.tips: In monsoon the ferry is sometimes cancelled (rough seas June to August). If the weather allows, take the first boat at 09:00 and bring a raincoat.
strings.d2.s1.name: Gateway of India Ferry Pier
strings.d2.s1.tips: For the return trip. Elephanta has only snacks.
strings.d2.s2.name: Britannia & Co Ballard Estate
strings.d2.s2.tips: A Parsi cafe from 1923. Try the berry pulao. Closed on Sundays and shuts at 16:00.
strings.d2.s3.name: Marine Drive
strings.d2.s3.tips: The "Queen's Necklace", a 3.6 km seafront. Walk from Nariman Point to Chowpatty at sunset as the street lamps come on.
strings.d2.s4.name: Girgaon Chowpatty Beach
strings.d2.s4.tips: Bhel puri and pav bhaji stalls line the beach. Swimming is not allowed.
strings.d2.b0.name: Kanheri Caves Sanjay Gandhi
strings.d2.b0.tips: If the ferry is cancelled: 109 Buddhist caves in the national park, near Borivali.
strings.d2.b1.name: Cafe Mondegar Colaba
strings.d2.b1.tips: A cafe with Mario Miranda murals. Beer and sandwiches.
strings.d3.s0.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
strings.d3.s0.tips: A UNESCO-listed Victorian Gothic station handling 3 million passengers a day. See it from outside and in the main hall.
strings.d3.s1.name: Dhobi Ghat Mahalaxmi
strings.d3.s1.tips: The world's largest open-air laundry. View it from the bridge; a tour costs 200 INR.
strings.d3.s2.name: Haji Ali Dargah
strings.d3.s2.tips: A tomb in the sea dating from 1431. The causeway is walkable at low tide. Expect loudspeaker chanting; cover your head.
strings.d3.s3.name: Haji Ali Juice Centre
strings.d3.s3.tips: The legendary juice stall across the way. Try the sitaphal (custard apple) cream.
strings.d3.s4.name: Mani Bhavan Gandhi Museum
strings.d3.s4.tips: Gandhi's Mumbai home from 1917 to 1934, in Gamdevi. Free entry.
strings.d3.b0.name: Shree Thaker Bhojanalay Kalbadevi
strings.d3.b1.name: Mahalaxmi Temple
strings.d3.b1.tips: A seaside temple, a substitute for Haji Ali at high tide.
strings.d4.s0.name: Dharavi Slum Tour Reality Tours
strings.d4.s0.tips: Asia's largest slum, with recycling, leather and pottery workshops. A responsible tour: no photos, and 80% of proceeds go to the community.
strings.d4.s1.name: Mahim Dargah
strings.d4.s2.name: Sarvi Byculla
strings.d4.s2.tips: Seekh kebab and khichda since the 1920s, in Byculla.
strings.d4.s3.name: Banganga Tank
strings.d4.s3.tips: A sacred tank on Malabar Hill dating from 1127, a village-like corner of Mumbai.
strings.d4.s4.name: Hanging Gardens Malabar Hill
strings.d4.s4.tips: Topiary shrubs and views of Marine Drive. The shoe-shaped house is in Kamala Nehru Park.
strings.d4.b0.name: Bhau Daji Lad Museum Byculla
strings.d4.b0.tips: The city's oldest museum in Byculla, a substitute for Banganga.
strings.d4.b1.name: Swati Snacks Tardeo
strings.d4.b1.tips: A Gujarati street-food restaurant: panki and dahi puri.
strings.d5.s0.name: Mount Mary Basilica
strings.d5.s0.tips: A basilica on Bandra hill. The Bandra Fair takes place in September.
strings.d5.s1.name: Bandstand Promenade
strings.d5.s1.tips: A seafront walk past Shah Rukh Khan's Mannat, with views of the Sea Link from Bandra Fort.
strings.d5.s2.name: Candies Bandra
strings.d5.s2.tips: A garden cafe serving Parsi and Goan dishes, a city favourite.
strings.d5.s3.name: Linking Road & Hill Road
strings.d5.s3.tips: A street market for cheap shoes and clothes.
strings.d5.s4.name: Carter Road Sunset
strings.d5.s4.tips: A rocky seafront promenade with Bandra's young crowd and cafes.
strings.d5.b0.name: Elco Bandra
strings.d5.b0.tips: A Hill Road institution for pani puri and chaat.
strings.d5.b1.name: Pali Village Cafe
strings.d5.b1.tips: An ivy-covered cafe on Pali Hill, best in the evening.
strings.d6.s0.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
strings.d6.s0.tips: Monsoon greenery and waterfalls. The paths are muddy, so wear proper shoes.
strings.d6.s1.name: Kanheri Caves
strings.d6.s1.tips: 109 Buddhist caves dating from the 1st century BC to the 10th century. The park bus takes 20 minutes.
strings.d6.s2.name: Global Vipassana Pagoda
strings.d6.s2.tips: The world's largest stone dome, in Gorai. Take the ferry (from Borivali West); meditation is offered.
strings.d6.s3.name: Juhu Beach
strings.d6.s3.tips: The Bollywood beach: pav bhaji and gola stalls, and sunset. Swimming is not allowed.
strings.d6.s4.name: Prithvi Cafe Juhu
strings.d6.s4.tips: A theatre cafe with Irish coffee and keema pav. Come on a play night.
strings.d6.b0.name: Anand Stall Juhu
strings.d6.b0.tips: Street-side vada pav and dosa opposite Mithibai College.
strings.d6.b1.name: ISKCON Juhu
strings.d6.b1.tips: A Hare Krishna temple, a nearby substitute for the pagoda.
strings.d7.theme: Fort morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Asiatic Society Library Town Hall
strings.d7.s0.tips: An 1830 neoclassical building on Horniman Circle. Its steps are a Bollywood set.
strings.d7.s1.name: Horniman Circle Gardens
strings.d7.s1.tips: A garden and St Thomas Cathedral (1718).
strings.d7.s2.name: Kyani & Co Marine Lines
strings.d7.s2.tips: A 1904 Irani cafe. Order bun maska and chai, or keema, for a farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Ashok Vada Pav Dadar
strings.d7.s3.tips: The city's most famous vada pav (potato fritter in a bun), by Kirti College.
strings.d7.s4.name: Mumbai Airport Metro/Taxi
strings.d7.s4.tips: Uber or Ola takes 45 to 90 minutes in traffic. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Yazdani Bakery Fort
strings.d7.b0.tips: An Irani bakery from 1953: brun maska.
strings.d7.b1.name: Flora Fountain
strings.d7.b1.tips: The fountain on Fort's square, a substitute for the gardens.
strings.note0: Use Uber/Ola (air-conditioned) or black-and-yellow taxis (metered). Suburban trains are packed; the first carriage is for women. Metro Line 3 has linked Colaba, Bandra and the airport since 2025. Allow 45 to 90 minutes to the airport in traffic.
strings.note1: JUNE TO SEPTEMBER MONSOON: hours of downpour daily, flooding, and the Elephanta ferry is sometimes cancelled. Bring an umbrella and sandals. The city is green and cool (28°C), and hotels are cheap.
strings.note2: The e-Visa (30 days) is applied for online. Carry cash in INR (with 500 notes in small change); UPI is limited for foreigners, and cards are accepted at larger places.
strings.note3: Street food: vada pav 20 to 30 INR, pav bhaji 100 INR, bhel puri 60 INR. Irani cafe breakfast 300 INR; restaurants 600 to 1,000 INR. Stick to bottled water and be careful with ice and raw salad.
strings.note4: Elephanta is closed on Mondays and Britannia on Sundays. Visit Haji Ali at low tide. Museums open at 10:15.
strings.note5: Visit Dharavi only with a responsible company (Reality Tours). A Bollywood studio tour (Film City) costs 2,000+ INR.
